text: Names at least five candidate frictions, each tied to a specific artifact in the snapshot
Identifies the shared pattern across both scripts: an unconditional success line appended after a command whose exit status is never checked, so every job reports success while failing
Selects the success-reporting pattern (or an equivalent cross-job fix) over the single-job fix of the Postgres connection error, and justifies it by the number of jobs it covers
Shows explicit multi-tier why-chain reasoning rather than jumping straight from symptom to fix
Names the runner-up problem and states why it lost
Notes the anomaly that index-notes exits 0 but is also run by hand, or that it never runs on schedule, rather than treating an exit-0 job as healthy
Delivers an actual script or tool, in a fenced code block, not a list of recommendations
Output closes with a report covering what was audited, why this problem over the alternatives, and how to run the tool
States separately what was verified and what was not, rather than asserting the fix works
